thesis_text:
Bottom line: for Notion (Notion Labs, Inc.) (SWE, entry), your odds through the cold application alone are low, but not zero. This read rests on a curated-qualitative record as of 2026-ten-twelve with no population sample — treat every pattern below as reported, not measured. High craft bar with a product-engineer (not pure-algorithm) flavour: the sourced posting screens for problem decomposition, UI quality, data-model fluency and business pragmatism in roughly equal weight, and the company is in-person (see red_flags). Experienced roles are senior-leaning (eight+ years on the sourced posting).

Who gets in (sample N=not available — curated-qualitative record, as of 2026-ten-twelve):
- This CIR is curated-qualitative: no population sample exists for it yet, so there are no percentages to show. What follows is the reported pattern from public sources, labeled as such.
Known biases of this data: Public postings describe the roles a company is currently trying to fill, not the people it actually hired; interview-prep and review sites are self-selected candidate reports; no licensed population dataset (PDL/Coresignal-class) was available for this record, so no school/employer/major shares are stated. Notion-specific: the posting mirror may lag the live posting; salary ranges are for SF and will differ by location/level.. We see who got in, not who tried and failed — survivorship bias is real (§0).

What Notion (Notion Labs, Inc.) says it screens for vs what the record shows:
Stated: In-person company: the posting states employees come in on two Anchor Days (Mondays and Thursdays) - a real location/attendance screen for many roles Writing and communication quality is an explicit screening capability ('empathetic communication', explaining technical decisions in writing) Product/craft sensibility: familiarity with computing-pioneer design ideas is listed as a bonus, signalling taste/craft screening - stated signal, weight unknown
Revealed: 

Routes in, ranked for you:
First: Direct application to a posted SWE role (Greenhouse-style posting) — See route details.
Second: Referral — See route details.
Third: Intern/new-grad program — See route details.

- school: you — not on file | cohort — See the school pattern in this CIR — stated qualitatively unless the CIR is population-backed; school is not in the user's control, so the plan routes around it (§three.1). | gap | fix: Do not plan around changing schools; offset with experience, projects and referrals.
- experience: you — no internships yet | cohort — High craft bar with a product-engineer (not pure-algorithm) flavour: the sourced posting screens for problem decomposition, UI quality, data-model fluency and business pragmatism in roughly equal weight, and the company is in-person (see red_flags). Experienced roles are senior-leaning (eight+ years on the sourced posting). | gap | fix: Land one real internship or role at a smaller, reachable employer first — the ladder pattern in this CIR's path patterns.
- projects: you — no projects on file | cohort — Revealed screen in this CIR: evidence of building or analyzing real things (see screening_signals.revealed). | gap | fix: Ship one project that solves a messy real problem for a real user, and document it.
- skills: you — no skills on file | cohort — not on file | unknown
- timing: you — year not on file | cohort — No official cadence published. Postings appear role-by-role rather than in a single annual new-grad cohort window, based on the posting set seen; re-verify each cycle. | unknown
- authorization: you — not on file | cohort — Sponsorship history is a matter of public record (DOL H-1B LCA filings); this CIR states only what its sources support, and immigration specifics go to the school's international office (§four.8 Q26 — not legal advice). | gap | fix: Confirm sponsorship for this exact role family before investing a season of prep; target employers with a filing history for the role.

The plan:
Next thirty days:
- Confirm this cycle's application window and deadlines for Notion (Notion Labs, Inc.) on the official careers page — dates move, and this CIR's cadence fact is the starting point, not the truth (§three.3). (by 2026-ten-19)
- Apply to a first, reachable rung: a smaller employer in the same role family (the ladder pattern in this CIR's path patterns). Volume plus follow-up is the play. (by 2026-ten-26)
- Ship the first version of one real project and write it up publicly. (by 2026-11-11)
- Build the coffee-chat target list from this CIR's entry routes: recent hires in the same role family, alumni of your school, people one rung up the ladder. (by 2026-ten-22)
This semester:
- Convert the semester into signal: one internship or substantial project, one visible leadership or club role in the field, and interview reps on a weekly schedule.
- Run the coffee-chat list: short, specific asks; every conversation ends with a follow-up you actually send.
This year:
- Be in the application pool for Notion (Notion Labs, Inc.)'s main entry window with the ladder rung, the project write-up and the referral conversations already done — not started.
- If the direct route misses, take the highest adjacent rung this CIR names and re-aim with a year of signal (the risks-and-alternatives route in this thesis).

Coffee-chat strategy: target the profile types named in the ranked routes — recent hires in this role family, alumni of your school now inside, and people one rung up the ladder you are climbing. Ask what the interviews actually test, what surprised them after starting, and what they would do with a semester to prepare. Keep asks short and specific; send the follow-up you promised.

Timeline and key dates: No official cadence published. Postings appear role-by-role rather than in a single annual new-grad cohort window, based on the posting set seen; re-verify each cycle. (as of 2026-ten-twelve; recruiting dates shift every cycle — re-check the official careers page before acting, §three.3).

Risks and alternatives: In-person expectation (Anchor Days) is a hard constraint for relocation-averse candidates - confirm per-role before investing prep time. No public official interview-process page found: any detailed stage-by-stage claim about Notion's loop circulating online is third-party and may be stale. Senior-leaning SWE postings (eight+ years on the sourced role) mean new-grad odds via cold application are likely low - say so honestly per Doc three s3. Adjacent options with similar signal: the other employers and role families whose CIRs share this ladder — the first rung matters more than the logo on it.
